answer: Registration runs on a quadratic bonding curve. The nth identity from one funding cluster locks 5 + 0.00002n² tokens, and clusters are found by tracing funding transactions three hops back through a Merkle index. A VRF then assigns each newcomer a sealed replay audit, and failure forfeits the lock. To forge 10,000 clones from one wallet tree, an attacker must freeze about 6.7 million tokens, roughly $670,000 at $0.10, for 90 days. An honest agent locks 5 tokens, refunded after audit. The price face steepens as sand does on a dune, so the lone climber reaches the terrace cheaply.
